question: What is the effective discount per cent (rounded off to 2 decimal places) if a shopkeeper offers a scheme, “buy five and get one free”?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a “Buy X Get Y Free” scheme, the discount percentage is calculated directly based on the free items.

Effective Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100

Here, Free items = 1 and Total items = 5 + 1 = 6

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 6) × 100 = 16.666...% ≈ 16.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Scheme: “Buy 5, Get 1 Free”

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount Amount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) of 1 item be 10 units.

⇒ Total items given to the customer = 5 + 1 = 6 items.

⇒ Total MP of 6 items = 6 × 10 = 60 units.

⇒ The customer only pays for 5 items, so Selling Price (SP) = 5 × 10 = 50 units.

⇒ Discount Amount = Total MP − SP = 60 − 50 = 10 units.

⇒ Effective Discount % = (10 ÷ 60) × 100 = 100 ÷ 6 = 16.666...%

⇒ Rounded off to two decimal places, the discount is 16.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free

The effective discount percentage is always calculated on the total number of items taken by the customer. Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the single equivalent discount is given by: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) is obtained after subtracting the discount: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].
